question: How does Raymond James's affiliation-choice model work commercially?

claims.text: The 2025 10-K (FY ended 2025-09-30) states that the firm offers multiple affiliation options, which it calls AdvisorChoice®. Advisors primarily affiliate directly as employees or independent contractors, or as employees of third-party RIAs and broker-dealers served through its RIA and Custody Services (RCS) division.

The 2025 10-K reports that the PCG segment had $1.67 trillion of client assets under administration, $1.01 trillion of it fee-based, and 8,943 employee and independent contractor financial advisors as of September 30, 2025.

The 2025 10-K describes employee advisors as working in a traditional branch supported by local management and administrative staff. They serve predominantly retail clients. Their compensation primarily includes a payout on revenues they generate, and they take part in the firm's employee benefit plans.

The recruiting page (content as of 2026-04-21) lists five AdvisorChoice® options: Traditional Employee (book ownership), Advisor Select, Independent Contractor, Bank & Credit Union, and Corporate RIA. The firm describes each as offering a different mix of support, freedom and flexibility.
The Traditional Employee page (content as of 2026-05-16) pitches book ownership and says there are no quotas and no product pushing.

The Advisor Select page (content as of 2026-03-11) calls it an employee affiliation option. Advisors get the employee channel's benefits and build their own branch. They choose a location, build out the office and run the branch P&L "to earn a higher rate on production."

The affiliation-options page (content as of 2026-04-21) sets entry qualifications, payout and compliance responsibility for each model. Bank & Credit Union needs a minimum of 3 years of experience and $250,000 in production. Compensation comes from the financial institution in partnership with Raymond James, and the branch manager and home office provide compliance support. Corporate RIA needs a minimum of 3 years of experience and $50 million in assets under advisement. It lists an 81% to 90% payout, and the divisional team and home office provide compliance support.

The same page (content as of 2026-04-21) says RIA & Custody Services requires $100 million or more in assets to establish a new RIA, a minimum of $30 million to plug in an existing RIA, and $1 billion or more in assets under management for introducing broker/dealers. Compensation is worked out with the RIA or broker/dealer, the advisor creates their own benefits package, and the advisor is responsible for compliance.

The Bank and Credit Union page (content as of 2026-05-17) cites 940 advisors across 160 financial institutions, $166 million average AUM per advisor and $950k average advisor production. It also says the Financial Institutions Division has operated since 1987.

The independent-advisor page (content as of 2026-05-19) says the Corporate RIA model lets fee-based advisors get the RIA experience while streamlining many of its burdens. It also lists business consulting (real estate, insurance, operations, structure) and business solutions (talent source, paraplanning, admin extension) for independent advisors.

The RIA and custody services page (content as of 2026-07-12) cites RCS principals' self-reported AUM: over 95% report $100 million, and portfolios average $475M. It also says nearly nine in 10 principals rate their RCS experience as positive.

On the 4Q25 earnings call (published 2026-01-28), CEO Paul Shoukry said the firm has "the largest addressable market across our affiliation options, from employee to independent contractor to the RIA custody." He said it has critical mass and decades of experience in all of them, and that advisors come from wires, regionals and other independents.

The 10-Q for the quarter ended 2025-12-31 (published 2026-02-06) says the firm offers loans to prospective financial advisors for recruiting and retention. The offers are contingent on events including the individuals joining or continuing their affiliation and meeting other conditions in the offer.

On the 2Q26 earnings call (published 2026-07-22), Shoukry said the firm is "agnostic" about how an advisor affiliates. Management wants advisors to fall in love with the culture, values and platform, and is "indifferent" to the affiliation route. He cited a 97% adviser satisfaction rate and said retention is the foundation for growth.

On the same 2Q26 call, Shoukry said the recruiting pipeline is strong across the affiliation options. His example was a team with $5 million of production that was weighing the pros and cons of each option after deciding Raymond James was the right partner.

The 2025 10-K lists risks tied to recruiting. Competitors frequently claim unfair hiring practices, and the firm has been subject to several such claims. The firm participates, with limited exceptions, in the voluntary Protocol for Broker Recruiting. The 10-K says the Protocol governs client information advisors may take and their ability to solicit prior clients, and that competitors may withdraw from it.

adjacent.text: WealthManagement.com (2026-10-29) reports that Shoukry told the fiscal fourth-quarter call that recruited advisors in the domestic independent contractor and employee channels had trailing 12-month production of $538 million, up from $407 million, and more than $82 billion in client assets. It says the independent contractor channel draws the most dollar interest, and quotes him saying advisors "don't have to select" a channel before judging cultural fit.
adjacent.differs_because: Trade-press reporting is indicative, not authoritative.

gaps.what: Raymond James: Headline payout ranges are published (company recruiting page, as of 2026-04-21); the full payout grid is not public. Only the Corporate RIA range (81% to 90%) appears in the evidence. Payout percentages for the Traditional Employee, Advisor Select and Independent Contractor options are not in the evidence provided.
gaps.suggested_source: Raymond James advisor recruiting pages for each affiliation option, or the 10-K PCG compensation discussion

gaps.what: The evidence provided does not give the revenue or profit split by affiliation channel, or the cost of recruiting loans by channel. It therefore does not show how the options differ in economics to the firm.
gaps.suggested_source: Raymond James 10-K/10-Q PCG segment and advisor-loan notes, or investor day deck

gaps.what: The 10-K description of independent contractor advisors is cut off in the evidence provided.
